title: Resuming a 10 GB upload
description: Someone is uploading a 10 GB video over hotel Wi-Fi that drops every few minutes. Later, they edit just 1 MB in the middle of another similar 10 GB file. Which upload design handles both interrupted transfers and small edits efficiently?

options.text: Stream the file through the API servers, which buffer it and write it to object storage once complete
options.explanation: Every drop restarts the transfer, app servers pay for all the bandwidth and memory, and the 1 MB edit still re-sends 10 GB.

options.text: One presigned PUT URL for the whole file, retried from the start on failure
options.explanation: Bytes bypass the servers, but a single 10 GB PUT rarely survives a flaky network and the small edit still re-uploads everything.

options.text: Split the file into chunks keyed by SHA-256, ask the server which hashes are missing, upload only those via presigned URLs, then commit the revision
options.explanation: Each chunk retries independently, a crashed upload resumes by re-asking which hashes are missing, and the edit uploads only the few changed chunks; the commit makes the revision visible atomically.

options.text: Upload the file over a WebSocket and have the server ack every 1 MB so the client can resume
options.explanation: It can resume, but bytes still flow through stateful app servers and there is no deduplication, so the 1 MB edit re-sends the whole file.
